ra: Arius is a foundational ancient heresiarch in the heterodox collective.
Nestorius is an ancient heresiarch in the heterodox collective.
Pelagius is an ancient heresiarch in the heterodox collective.
Donatus is an ancient schismatic/heresiarch in the heterodox collective.
Montanus is an ancient heresiarch in the heterodox collective.
Priscillian is an ancient heresiarch in the heterodox collective.
Eutyches is an ancient heresiarch in the heterodox collective.
Sabellius is an ancient heresiarch in the heterodox collective.
The Bogomils are a medieval dualist movement in the heterodox collective.
The Cathar Perfecti are a medieval dualist movement in the heterodox collective.
The Paulicians are a medieval dualist movement in the heterodox collective.
Peter Waldo is a medieval heresiarch/founder in the heterodox collective.
The Waldensians are a medieval dissenting movement in the heterodox collective.
The Bosnian Church is a medieval dissenting body in the heterodox collective.
Athanasius of Alexandria was the chief patristic opponent of Arius and Arianism after Nicaea.
Athanasius led the orthodox defense against Arius's subordinationist Christology.
The Waldensian movement received its origin and rule of apostolic poverty from Peter Waldo, its founder.
The Bogomils received and transmitted the dualist cosmology earlier carried by the Paulicians of the Byzantine East (Lambert).
Western Catharism received its dualist doctrine and ritual (the consolamentum) from Balkan Bogomilism (Lambert).
The Bosnian Church was widely (if contestedly) linked to Bogomil dualist influence by medieval polemicists (Lambert).
Paulician radical dualism was assimilated by Byzantine heresiologists to Manichaean dualism, of which Mani is the founder.
Medieval polemicists labelled the dualist Cathars 'Manichaeans'; their cosmology parallels Manichaean dualism.
Bernard of Clairvaux preached against the Cathar heretics of the Languedoc in 1145 (Lambert).
Bernard of Clairvaux led an early preaching campaign against Catharism.
Dominic's preaching mission and the founding of the Order of Preachers were directed against the Albigensian Cathars (Lambert).
Dominic founded his order to combat the Albigensian heresy.
Nestorius opposed the title Theotokos for Mary, rejecting it in favor of Christotokos, the dispute condemned at Ephesus.
